note: Items carry optional conditions: alt (only when the trek goes at least this high), cold, wet, snow, camping, porter (only in that situation). rent marks things that are easy to rent in Kathmandu or Pokhara.

items.t: Passport, plus two passport photos for permits
Permits and trekker registration card
items.n: Keep them where you can reach them at checkpoints.

items.t: Insurance policy number and 24-hour assistance phone, on paper
Nepali rupees in cash for the whole trek
items.n: ATMs are rare and unreliable once you leave the city.

items.t: Photocopies or phone photos of passport and visa
Emergency card filled in on this site
Day pack, 25–35 litres, with a rain cover
Soft duffel for the porter, 60–80 litres
items.n: Keep it to 10–12 kg so the porter's load stays within limits.

items.t: Trekking pack, 45–60 litres, if you carry everything yourself
Dry bags or strong plastic bags to line the pack
Small padlock for the duffel and lodge doors
Trekking boots you have already broken in
items.n: Do not rent or buy these new for the trek.

items.t: Three or four pairs of trekking socks
Thick warm socks for the evenings
Sandals or light shoes for lodges and river crossings
Gaiters
Microspikes
Two or three quick-drying base-layer tops
Trekking trousers, and shorts for the low valleys
Fleece or light insulated mid layer
Waterproof jacket with a hood
Waterproof overtrousers
Thick down jacket
Light down or synthetic jacket
Thermal leggings and top to sleep in
Warm hat that covers the ears
Sun hat or cap
Buff or scarf for dust, sun and cold air
Light gloves
Insulated gloves or mittens
Underwear, including one spare set kept dry
Poncho or pack-covering rain cape
Modest clothes for villages and monasteries
Sleeping bag rated to about −10 °C
Sleeping bag rated to −20 °C
Light sleeping bag or liner
Sleeping bag liner
items.n: Adds warmth and keeps a rented bag away from your skin.

items.t: Earplugs
Inflatable sleeping mat
Trekking poles
Headlamp with spare batteries
Sunglasses with full UV protection
Two one-litre water bottles, or a bottle and a bladder
Water treatment: tablets, filter or UV pen
Sunscreen SPF 50 and lip balm with SPF
Printed map of the region
Whistle
Snacks for the first days: nuts, bars, dried fruit
Insulated flask for hot water
Umbrella
items.n: Better than a jacket in warm monsoon rain.

items.t: Leech socks and salt
Personal first-aid kit: plasters, blister dressings, tape, antiseptic
Painkillers: paracetamol and ibuprofen
Oral rehydration salts and diarrhoea medicine
Your own prescription medicines, with spares in a separate bag
Altitude medicine, if a doctor has prescribed it for you
Pulse oximeter
items.n: A trend to watch, not a diagnosis. Symptoms matter more.

items.t: Hand sanitiser and soap
Toilet paper and a lighter or bags to carry it out
Quick-drying towel
Toothbrush, toothpaste and basic toiletries
Wet wipes
items.n: Showers get cold, scarce and expensive higher up.

items.t: Menstrual products, and bags to carry used ones out
Insect repellent
Phone with offline maps and this site saved
Power bank, 10,000 mAh or more
Charging cables and a plug adapter
items.n: Nepal uses round two- and three-pin sockets.

items.t: Local SIM card
items.n: Carry both main networks on remote routes if you can.

items.t: Camera, spare battery and memory card
Solar panel or second power bank
Satellite messenger with an active plan
items.n: For routes several days from a road or phone signal.

items.t: Tent rated for the season
Stove, fuel and cooking pots
Mug, bowl and spoon
Repair kit: tape, cord, needle and thread
Crampons, ice axe and rope, if the route crosses a glacier
items.n: And a guide who knows how to use them.
